newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - LME copper eyes stubborn upside.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - LME copper eyes stubborn upside.

text.p: Base metals face stubborn upside resistance this week on the London Metal Exchange (LME) as business thins ahead of the Easter holiday, analysts said.
Copper, which has spent the past two weeks in a broad $2,300-$2,380 range, failed in another bid to break out higher on Friday.
But Friday's kerb close of $2,368 per tonne was still positive -- particularly considering copper's dramatic recovery from near $2,300 on Wednesday.
In the immediate term, a firmer cash to threes backwardation above $50 was supportive of copper, as was Friday's near 10,000-tonne LME stocks drawdown.
Tuesday's inventory report will be watched closely to seen whether last Friday's shipment of some 6,000 tonnes of copper to China from the LME warehouse in Singapore is repeated.
"What people are questioning is whether this is the start of a new import spree from China like we saw in September, October and November last year," said analyst Robin Bhar of brokers Brandeis.
Market holidays this Friday and next Monday will reduce volumes and and may lead to whippy trading conditions.
"Trading will be in a low ebb as people decide whether to go into market or wait until April Fool's Day after the Easter holiday," Bhar noted.
On the charts, the 14-day RSI is neutral at around 56 percent, while the downtrending 10-day moving average and upwards-heading 30-day indicator appear to be flattening out.

"Recent retreats have allowed the earlier overbought condition to unwind and prices are well placed to recognise supports immediately below $2,300 now," said technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
"However, there are no signs of a further bout of substantial strength developing here yet."
Aluminium similarly has been consolidating below recent highs around $1,675, a level which needs to be hurdled before the metal can advance, analysts said.
But any upward ambitions in the aluminium market have been foiled recently by Far Eastern and producer forward selling, dealers said.
LME stocks will also factor strongly in aluminium, with dealers expecting large drawdowns this week.
Zinc, arguably the most buoyant of the non-ferrous metals, will be struggling to better its recent high of $1,307. It finished Friday's kerb off lows at $1,297.
"Despite overbought considerations, the move could go even further yet. The medium term target is $1,400 still," Gifford said. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
